topic: Flight Recorder held-out scenario identity, external-eval import integrity, and claim-authorization boundary

facts: The README describes Flight Recorder as a deterministic evidence/governance layer and explicitly separates evaluation from promotion/governance claims.
The architecture table states Eval requires identical held-out scenarios, adapter contracts, imported per-case execution evidence, and separation between raw movement and governance claims.
Each suite source is projected to unique scenario IDs plus per-scenario scenario_sha256 fingerprints.
The manifest blocks duplicate scenario IDs, missing fingerprints, failed fingerprint replay, duplicate source labels/paths/content, scenario-set mismatch, and scenario-fingerprint mismatch.

cross_arm_claims_allowed becomes true only when multiple sources have identical held-out scenario IDs and matching fingerprints; a single ready source can seed an external plan but cannot authorize cross-arm claims.
Manifest publication rechecks captured source snapshots and uses CAS-style atomic JSON publication so source mutation between build and write is not silently accepted.
External-eval plans bind each adapter execution contract to scenario_manifest_sha256.
Plan readiness never itself enables external-eval claims: governance_handoff.external_eval_claims_allowed is hard-coded false, and semantic validation rejects a plan that attempts to set it true.
The plan/receipt layer is explicitly dry-run/readiness governance and does not launch benchmark code.
Imported external results bind plan, held-out manifest, raw result and optional runner-metadata SHA-256 identities into a result identity digest.
The importer requires the plan's held-out-manifest hash to equal the imported held-out manifest hash.

Completed execution requires duplicate-free finite per-case raw records, supported normalizer contract, coherent runner exit status, exact expected/observed/mapped case coverage, and a conclusive benchmark outcome; aggregate-only output is insufficient.
Claims are allowed only after integrity passes, execution is completed, exact coverage is complete, benchmark outcome is passed, and credential-recording side effects are not observed.

scope_limited_findings.claim: Flight Recorder provides direct public implementation evidence for a claim-authorization split: a ready evaluation plan is not authority to make evaluation claims, and raw/aggregate movement is insufficient. Claim authority is downstream of scenario/content identity, imported per-case evidence, exact coverage and integrity checks.
scope_limited_findings.scope: Evaluation-governance infrastructure, not a scientist-agent memory or tool-routing performance ablation.

scope_limited_findings.claim: Cross-arm comparability is content-bound rather than label-bound: matching scenario IDs alone are insufficient when per-scenario SHA-256 fingerprints differ, and a single held-out source cannot authorize a cross-arm claim.
scope_limited_findings.scope: Flight Recorder held-out manifest semantics at revision 5172267...

scope_limited_findings.claim: External evaluation evidence remains non-authoritative until the exact held-out manifest hash, raw per-case result, runner observation/metadata, normalizer contract and coverage are imported and bound. This is a strong analog for scientific-agent evidence handoff rules that separate execution/readiness artifacts from downstream acceptance authority.
scope_limited_findings.scope: Analogical protocol support only; no claim that Flight Recorder validates scientific conclusions or autonomous-science causal effects.

next_actions: Inspect the repository's public case-study artifacts only if they add an already-executed exact duplicate/freshness challenge relevant to replay provenance; otherwise avoid duplicating existing protocol semantics.
Resume the stronger unresolved science-domain frontier: an already-published fixed-memory/same-selected-identity receiver-effect intervention or a Table-3 provenance bridge for MemCompiler.
Keep Flight Recorder as external protocol corroboration, not as causal evidence for scientist-agent benchmark gains.
